original_question: Consider a torus T 2 bundle over S. Under what hypothesis on the monodromy ρ can we find a foliation with no compact leaves close to a fiber?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Question 4.4, the open problem about a torus T^2-bundle over S and which monodromies allow a nearby foliation without compact leaves near a fiber; Questions 4.2 and 4.3 supply the intended setup and nearby reformulation. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s core content very well: the total space is a torus T^2-bundle over S, the dependence is on the monodromy ρ, and the question is existential—whether one can find a nearby foliation with no compact leaves near a fiber—so it matches Question 4.4 rather than the universal persistence problem in Question 4.2. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: You should name the reference foliation F explicitly: it is the foliation of the total space by the torus fibers of the bundle, and the new foliation is required to be close to that specific foliation. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The relevant notion of closeness is not stated in your draft; the surrounding discussion uses the C^1-nearby setting for foliations/vector fields. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Your draft does not identify ρ as the bundle monodromy. In the nearby reformulation, this is written as a representation ρ: π1(S) → SL(2, Z). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The base surface assumptions are implicit in your draft. Nearby context takes S to be a closed orientable surface; the vector-field reformulation assumes genus > 1, while Question 4.2 specializes to the genus-2 case. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The intended geometric meaning is that a small perturbation can 'open' the torus fibers, i.e. produce a nearby foliation with no compact leaves near fibers, not merely eliminate one isolated compact leaf. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: Let π: M → S be a torus T^2-bundle over a closed surface S, with bundle monodromy ρ, and let F be the foliation of M by the torus fibers of π. Under what hypotheses on ρ does there exist a foliation G that is C^1-close to F and has no compact leaves close to a fiber of π? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 4.1, Question 4.4 (page 17), because it asks for the existence of a nearby compact-leaf-free foliation. Question 4.2 asks the opposite universal/persistence version—whether every nearby foliation must retain a compact leaf near a fiber—while the text around Questions 4.2–4.4 explains the monodromy-based motivation, the C^1-nearby viewpoint, and the examples contrasting trivial monodromy with cyclic hyperbolic monodromy. The paper also says that Question 4.3 is 'essentially equivalent' to Question 4.4, but it does not provide a formal proof of equivalence there, so no alternate formulation is supplied. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
